Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you
reported. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by my initials for this one, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the collision happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, near a shopping center. Traffic was light and it was a clear
afternoon.
Q: What were you doing right before impact?
A: I was heading toward the intersection and slowed down for a car ahead that was turning. The other vehicle came
over into my lane. I braked, but we still met nose to nose.
Q: How fast were you traveling when the vehicles made contact?
A: Not fast at all. I'd guess under fifteen miles an hour. Nobody's airbags went off, and both cars were still drivable,
though they were towed.
Q: Did you feel any injury at the scene?
A: Not right away. I felt a little stiff in the neck, but I figured it would pass. By that evening the pain had gotten worse,
mostly on the left side, and I had trouble turning my head to check mirrors.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I saw my family doctor the next morning. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a
referral for physical therapy. I've been going twice a week.
Q: Have you had any neck problems before this collision?
A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that stopped me from working
or sleeping.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and get my records to you as soon as possible.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
